articles.title: Emerging insights into amino acid metabolism in the heart: implications for cardiovascular diseases and therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: As a metabolically versatile organ, the heart is capable of generating energy from a wide range of substrates. Although fatty acid and glucose metabolism in the heart have been extensively studied, the contribution of amino acid metabolism to cardiac physiology and disease is gaining increasing attention. A range of amino acids, including branched-chain amino acids, glutamine and glutamate, asparagine, glycine, tryptophan and alanine, play integral roles in signalling pathways that orchestrate key adaptive and maladaptive changes in the myocardium, under both physiological and pathological stress. Dysregulation of these pathways is associated with cardiovascular disease such as heart failure, hypertension, myocardial infarction and atherosclerosis, via mechanisms involving impaired mitochondrial function, oxidative stress and inflammation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of amino acid metabolism in the heart, including sulphur amino acids, their role in relation to cardiovascular disease and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting amino acid metabolism in the heart. Finally, this review also discusses current and ongoing clinical trials targeting amino acid metabolism with the aim of finding potential therapeutic targets in cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: The fight of innate immunity and abnormal cannabinoids against Candida infection.
articles.abstract: Candida species represent the most clinically significant fungal pathogens in humans, with invasive candidiasis carrying a mortality of 30%-40% in critically ill patients despite modern antifungal therapy. The innate immune system - through the coordinated and specific activities of neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, mast cells and eosinophils - constitute the primary and most consequential biological defence against Candida invasion. Abnormal cannabinoids (Abn-CBDs), a structurally distinctive class of synthetic lipid compounds with non-psychoactive properties and regioisomeric configurations, critically distinct from classical cannabinoids in their independence from CB1 and CB2 receptor signalling, have emerged as a novel and pharmacologically compelling class of antifungal compounds. This review integrates the current understanding of innate immune cell antifungal mechanisms with the emerging pharmacology of abnormal cannabinoids, examines the direct antifungal and immunomodulatory properties of Abn-CBDs, and critically addresses the tripartite contest between innate immunity, abnormal cannabinoids and Candida's formidable evasion repertoire.

articles.title: Needle-free jet injection in translation: a narrative review of the state of the art, key trends, and research gaps.
articles.abstract: Needle-free jet injectors (NFJIs) deliver drugs through high-velocity liquid microjets that penetrate skin without needles, offering potential advantages in patient acceptability, sharps waste reduction, and intradermal targeting. We reviewed recent translational evidence for NFJIs with emphasis on commercially-accessible spring- and gas-powered systems. A PubMed search yielded 12,364 records; 351 articles were assessed for eligibility and 143 studies (2010- February 2025) were included for analysis, with figures summarizing investigation frequency and publication count. Across studies, spring-powered devices were evaluated more evenly across in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo stages, whereas gas-powered systems were more frequently studied in clinical trials, with comparatively limited ex vivo assessment. Commonly-investigated parameters were nozzle diameters of 150-200 μm and intradermal injection volumes of 50-100 μL. Jet performance and safety were strongly influenced by pressure/velocity, stand-off distance, formulation viscosity, and skin mechanics; velocities of ~100 m/s are frequently cited as a threshold for reliable penetration, while excessive pressure can increase splash-back and tissue trauma. Despite expanding applications e.g., vaccination, anesthesia, dermatologic intralesional therapies, translation is hindered by inconsistent reporting of jet parameters and limited standardized, quantitative endpoints. We propose that harmonized reporting and assessment methods should integrate model selection, parameter documentation, and clinically meaningful endpoints. With these key improvements reproducibility and acceleration of NFJI adoption can be achieved.

articles.title: Nanoparticles for cardiovascular diseases: identifying and overcoming barriers in translating preclinical success to clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Nanoparticles (NPs) have emerged as versatile platforms for drug delivery in cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), demonstrating robust efficacy in preclinical models by stabilizing atherosclerotic plaques, promoting safe and efficient thrombolysis, and mitigating ischemia-reperfusion injury. These advances highlight the maturation of cardiovascular nanomedicine; however, translation to clinical practice remains limited. This gap between laboratory success and clinical adoption reflects broader challenges in nanomedicine design, including suboptimal delivery to diseased tissues, limited efficacy of single therapeutic payload-based strategies in addressing the multifaceted inflammatory pathways driving CVDs, NPs' immunogenicity, and scale-up feasibility. Addressing these barriers is particularly critical in CVDs, where therapeutic success depends on precise engagement with multiple molecular and cellular drivers of disease. This review discusses the evolving landscape of cardiovascular nanomedicine, focusing on four aspects. First, we highlight advances in NPs bioengineering strategies, such as refined targeting moieties, optimized physicochemical properties, and responsiveness to endogenous and external stimuli that enhance organ- and cell-specific delivery in atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Second, we discuss analytical innovations that improve characterization and control of NPs' biodistribution, enabling more rational targeting. Third, we evaluate therapeutic payloads, emphasizing how RNA-based and immunomodulatory agents represent a meaningful step toward clinical translation. Fourth, we outline approaches to addressing persistent challenges in safety and scalable manufacturing. Together, these developments establish a foundation for translating NP design principles into practical cardiovascular therapies. With continued progress in targeted delivery, clinical safety, and production scalability, cardiovascular nanomedicine is increasingly well-positioned to translate preclinical advances to transformative patient outcomes.

articles.title: Use of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1 Receptor Agonists, and DPP-4 Inhibitors in Incident Hyponatremia in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Target Trial Emulations.
articles.abstract: Hyponatremia poses risks in type 2 diabetes, yet comparative electrolyte safety across glucose-lowering therapies remains unclear. We evaluated the risk of incident hyponatremia associated with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors in real-world practice. Using electronic health records from 155 healthcare organizations in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted multicenter active-comparator, new-user target trial emulations with 1:1 propensity score matching. For each pairwise comparison, adults with type 2 diabetes initiating either drug class, with no record of either class during the preceding 365 days, were included. The primary outcome was incident hyponatremia (ICD-10-CM E87.1 or serum sodium ≤ 135 mmol/L); sensitivity outcomes included diagnosis-only, laboratory-only, and stricter laboratory thresholds. Among more than 300,000 matched pairs per comparison, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were each associated with a 15% lower hazard of hyponatremia than DPP-4 inhibitors (hazard ratio [HR], 0.850; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.842-0.858 and HR, 0.847; 95% CI: 0.838-0.856). The lower risk persisted at stricter sodium thresholds and across clinically relevant subgroups, including patients with heart failure, chronic kidney disease, or high-risk medications use. SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were broadly comparable (HR, 0.962; 95% CI: 0.952-0.971). Positive and negative control outcomes were consistent with expectations. Overall, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were associated with a lower risk of incident hyponatremia than DPP-4 inhibitors. These real-world findings provide reassurance regarding the electrolyte safety of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs, complementing their established cardiorenal benefits.

The EMA Qualification Opinion for CYP Inhibition-Mediated Drug-Drug Interaction Predictions: Implications for PBPK Credibility Assessment in the Era of ICH M15.
articles.abstract: Clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics teams are now being encouraged to implement the ICH M15 framework in drug development to support model-informed decisions in regulatory submissions. Although model performance is an important component of model evaluation, regulatory confidence also depends on the intended context of use (CoU) and the supporting level of evidence. This is particularly relevant for physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, where increasing regulatory application has strengthened the need for structured approaches to evaluate predictive performance, extrapolation, uncertainty, and model applicability. The Simcyp Simulator (V19R1) was recently qualified by the EMA for prediction of CYP-mediated drug-drug interactions (DDIs) involving six enzymes (CYP1A2, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4/5), competitive inhibition, and mechanism-based inhibition for both victim and perpetrator drugs across three CoUs. Qualification data demonstrated consistent predictive performance across the three CoUs, with average fold errors close to unity, absolute average fold errors ranging from 1.23 to 1.25, and 98.8% of 246 predictions falling within 2-fold of observed values. The opinion predates ICH M15; however, it does not provide either a mapping to its credibility concepts or an operational basis for extending platform-level evidence to a specific investigational drug. We address this gap with an explicit mapping of the qualification opinion onto ICH M15 credibility concepts and an integrated approach linking qualification evidence, drug-specific validation, predictive performance, uncertainty characterization, and prospective application, illustrating how confidence in PBPK-supported regulatory decisions can be established within an ICH M15-aligned framework.

articles.title: November 2026 issue first authors.
Uncovering the lymphatic uptake, pharmacokinetics, and biodistribution of mRNA-lipid nanoparticles after intravenous and subcutaneous injection.
articles.abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations have enabled the in vivo delivery of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccines and therapeutics yet the delivery of RNA remains relatively inefficient. In order to improve LNP design there is a need to better understand how current mRNA-LNP formulations are trafficked and expressed in vivo. Importantly, no prior work has quantified mRNA-LNP transport through lymphatics. In the current study we profile the thoracic lymph uptake, plasma pharmacokinetics (PK), and tissue protein expression after intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration in rats of three common LNP formulations (ALC-0315, SM-102 and MC3 ionizable lipids) containing muGFP-P2A-nLuc reporter mRNA. After IV administration, the SM-102 and MC3 LNP formulations provided the most effective protection of mRNA in plasma. Despite this, tissue NanoLuc® Luciferase (nLuc) expression at 32 h post-dosing was relatively similar across formulations with highest expression seen in the liver and spleen. After SC injection, all formulations supported relatively low bioavailability of mRNA (0.42-0.87% dose) and slightly higher bioavailability of ionizable and PEG lipid (<5% dose) with PK profiles of the ionizable lipid and PEG lipid not completely matching the mRNA PK profiles. There was also greater lymphatic recovery of all ionizable lipids (3.1-4.3% dose) compared to mRNA (0.62-1.4% dose) and PEG lipid (1.9-2.0% dose). Together this data suggests that mRNA is lost prior to or during lymphatic transport. Importantly, concentrations of all mRNA-LNP components were 10-1000 fold higher in thoracic lymph compared to plasma after SC injection. At 32 h after SC injection, highest nLuc expression was seen in lymph nodes and tissues near the dosing site and in the liver and spleen. These findings demonstrating that mRNA-LNPs predominantly traffic from tissue injection sites via lymphatics, mRNA-LNP components may traffic separately from each other in both lymph and blood, and tissue protein expression reflects the PK of mRNA-LNPs at early timepoints.

articles.title: MAMDC2 drives microglia-mediated neuroinflammation via CAND1-dependent IκBα ubiquitination and is targetable by Artemvulactone E.
articles.abstract: Sustained microglial activation is a common feature of many neurological disorders, yet the upstream molecular amplifiers that sustain this process remain poorly defined. Our earlier work identified MAM domain-containing 2 (MAMDC2) as an immune regulator enriched in microglia with an established role in antiviral immunity. However, whether and how MAMDC2 shapes microglial inflammatory activation and neuroinflammation has remained largely unexplored. Here, we show that MAMDC2 is strongly induced in microglia after challenge with LPS or HSV-1, both in vitro and in vivo, where it amplifies the microglial inflammatory response. Mechanistically, MAMDC2 associates with Cullin-associated and neddylation-dissociated protein 1 (CAND1) and facilitates K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of IκBα, thereby enhancing NF-κB-dependent inflammatory signaling and activating the downstream JAK2-STAT1 pathway. In male mice, loss of MAMDC2 alleviated neuroinflammatory pathology and glial activation, and improved motor behavior. By combining virtual screening with experimental validation, we further identified Artemvulactone E (AE), a sesquiterpenoid from Artemisia vulgaris L., as a small molecule that targets MAMDC2. AE disrupts the MAMDC2-CAND1 interaction, thereby dampening NF-κB-dependent microglial inflammation and protecting against LPS-induced pathology in vivo. Together, these findings establish MAMDC2 as a previously unrecognized upstream amplifier of microglial inflammation acting through the CAND1-IκBα-NF-κB axis and identify AE as a promising pharmacological modulator of MAMDC2 for the treatment of neuroinflammatory disorders.

articles.title: Pariglasgene Brecaparvovec: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Pariglasgene brecaparvovec (GENGLYCOS™, pariglasgene brecaparvovec-opnr) is an adeno-associated virus serotype 8 (AAV8) vector gene therapy developed by Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical for the treatment of glycogen storage disease type Ia. As glycogen storage disease type Ia occurs due to defects in glucose-6-phosphatase, pariglasgene brecaparvovec delivers a functional copy of the G6PC gene to stabilise blood glucose levels and reduce cornstarch intake in patients. Pariglasgene brecaparvovec received an accelerated approval in the USA on 19 August 2026. This article summarises the milestones in the development of pariglasgene brecaparvovec leading to this first approval to reduce daily cornstarch intake as an adjunct to nutritional management in adult and paediatric patients ≥ 8 years of age with glycogen storage disease type Ia.

articles.title: Pathway-level secretome modulation in bronchial epithelial spheroids following indoor dust exposure.
articles.abstract: As humans spend most of their time indoors, they are continuously exposed to an array of indoor air pollutants. While exposure to individual indoor air pollutants may often occur at low levels, cumulative exposure to indoor air pollutants contributes substantially to the human exposome. Chronic inhalation of indoor air pollutants has been associated with multiple respiratory diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and respiratory infections. In this study, the cellular effects of an acute indoor dust exposure using a three-dimensional airway epithelial model were investigated. Bronchial epithelial cells (16HBE14o-) were cultured as spheroids and exposed to reference indoor dust (SRM 2585; 0-200 µg/mL) for 24 h. Metabolic activity, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and secretome profiles were assessed. Indoor dust exposure did not induce morphological alterations or significant reductions in metabolic activity. Instead, a concentration-dependent increase in intracellular ROS was observed. Cytokine analysis revealed selective cytokine modulation, while untargeted proteomics identified limited changes in individual protein abundance. Instead, pathway-level analyses revealed enrichment of epithelial differentiation-related pathways. Overall, these findings suggest that a 24 h indoor dust exposure may elicit subtle cellular responses rather than overt cytotoxicity or inflammatory activation. This study highlights the applicability of integrating functional, immunological, and proteomics-based approaches with 3D airway models to investigate cellular responses to complex environmental particle mixtures. However, direct extrapolation to human exposure scenarios is limited by uncertainties regarding effective cellular dose, particle localization and environmental representativeness. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory, hypothesis-generating observations.

articles.title: Advancing Therapeutics for Children with Medical Complexity: The Role of Model-Informed Precision Dosing and Genotype-Stratified Trials.
articles.abstract: Model-informed drug development (MIDD) and model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) increasingly guide drug development, regulatory decision-making, and individualized therapy but rely on robust data. Current models inadequately represent children with medical complexity (CMC), whose unique physiology, comorbidities, and polypharmacy contribute to substantial variability in drug exposure and response. We propose a framework using genotype-stratified trials to characterize pharmacogenetic sources of variability, informing MIDD and MPID models while helping identify additional determinants of therapeutic response in CMC.

articles.title: Quantitative Sciences in the Model-Informed Era: From Parallel Functions to a Shared Decision System.
articles.abstract: Model-informed drug development increasingly depends on collaboration among clinical pharmacology, statistics, pharmacometrics, and quantitative systems pharmacology. Yet functional silos, distinct leadership structures, and divergent goals can reduce collaboration to late, parallel deliverables that constrain decision architecture. This Perspective defines a shared decision system as an operating model in which quantitative and clinical disciplines jointly define the question, context of use, evidentiary role, uncertainty standards, and accountability for model-informed evidence.

articles.title: Advancing precision immune modulation.
Human cytochrome P450 27A1-a variety of reactions, applications, and potentials for drug targeting.
articles.abstract: The human cytochrome P450 (P450) 27A1 enzyme is most often described as a liver enzyme that initiates the alternative (acidic) pathway of bile acid synthesis. Although this is certainly an important role for this enzyme, research has shown that it has a significantly wider role to play in normal physiology and disease pathology. This minireview aims to provide a useful reference for studies showing the many ways P450 27A1 is involved in human health and to help researchers access useful methods. The distribution, expression, and regulation of the enzyme in both normal and disease states are discussed. A catalog of steady-state kinetics experiments is included. A review of methods for recombinant expression, inhibition, and studying redox partner interactions is also included. Two key examples of connections to disease, breast cancer and neurodegeneration, are explored as possible applications of P450 27A1 research and illustrations of the complexity of the role of the enzyme. Finally, a few key areas of needed clarification are suggested with hopes to inspire researchers to contribute to work in this important area. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Human cytochrome P450 27A1 and its products, particularly 27-hydroxycholesterol, are increasingly connected to variety of diseases such as cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis, atherosclerosis, multiple cancers, and neurodegenerative diseases. This review explores the systemic physiological control and basic enzymology of cytochrome P450 27A1 to facilitate collaboration across these different biomedical dimensions toward advancing diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Active Components in the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline and multifactorial pathology. Because AD involves interacting pathological processes, the limited efficacy of conventional single-target therapies has increased interest in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and other natural medicines with multi-target pharmacological actions. TCM-derived active components originate from medicinal materials used in traditional practice and are evaluated using modern pharmacological approaches. Their source medicines have diverse traditional-use backgrounds. Some have historical associations with memory or cognitive symptoms, whereas many others were traditionally used for broader deficiency, phlegm, blood-stasis, heat, or related syndromic patterns. These records provide ethnopharmacological context for the source medicines but should not be taken as historical evidence for the anti-AD activity of their isolated constituents. AIM OF THE REVIEW: This review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms of TCM-derived bioactive components in AD while incorporating relevant traditional-use information on their source medicines. Particular attention is given to their multi-target actions and emerging mechanisms involving ferroptosis, mitophagy, and the gut-brain axis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Mechanistic literature published between January 2019 and November 2025 was retrieved from Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. Ovid MEDLINE and PubMed were searched separately to maximize retrieval across indexed and additional PubMed records, with overlapping records removed during deduplication. Traditional-use information was evaluated separately for the source medicines. A targeted search of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov was also conducted to assess human interventional evidence for compounds covered in the review, with trial-registration information updated through August 2026. RESULTS: Current preclinical findings suggest that TCM active components may produce coordinated preclinical pharmacological effects through multiple pathways, including the inhibition of β-amyloid (Aβ) production and deposition, regulation of tau aggregation and phosphorylation, alleviation of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, improvement of mitophagy and iron metabolism disorders, and modulation of gut microbiota homeostasis. Among these components, saponins show broad mechanistic coverage. Flavonoids, polysaccharides, and other bioactive substances have likewise shown anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, together with protective effects on synaptic function, in preclinical models. These mechanistic findings were derived predominantly from cellular and animal studies, with computational analyses providing mainly hypothesis-generating support. Human evidence was available for only a small subset of compounds and was not uniformly positive. Huperzine A has progressed to controlled clinical testing but has shown mixed efficacy findings; resveratrol demonstrated CNS exposure and biomarker activity without consistent cognitive benefit; curcumin did not show efficacy in a placebo-controlled AD trial; and favorable signals from ginseng studies were limited by open-label designs and the use of whole preparations rather than isolated ginsenosides. CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence supports broad preclinical activity of TCM-derived components across several interconnected AD-related processes, but the strength of mechanistic support varies markedly among compounds and pathways. Human translation remains limited and inconsistent, and current clinical data do not establish disease-modifying efficacy for the compounds reviewed. Further development should therefore be guided by the main uncertainty surrounding each candidate-whether mechanistic causality, reproducibility, systemic or CNS exposure, preparation standardization, or clinical efficacy-rather than by a fixed sequence of technologies.

articles.title: In vitro dissolution testing of long-acting injectables: regulatory methods, mechanistic development, and In Vitro-In vivo correlations.
articles.abstract: Long-acting injectables (LAIs) have become an important platform for drug delivery providing sustained drug exposure over weeks to months, creating an increasing need for predictive in vitro dissolution methods to support formulation development, quality control, and the establishment of meaningful in vitro-in vivo correlations (IVIVCs). However, standardized in vitro release methods and regulatory guidance covering the range of LAI formulations remain limited, and existing recommendations vary across formulation types and regulatory authorities. This review examines FDA-recommended dissolution methods, relevant guidance from other regulatory authorities, and formulation-specific methodologies reported in the literature, and evaluates their applicability to the development of IVIVCs for LAIs. The available evidence demonstrates that current compendial methods primarily serve as product-specific quality control tests. Successful biopharmaceutically relevant dissolution testing depends on reproducing the dominant release mechanisms of each formulation platform, including drug dissolution, partitioning, polymer degradation, phase inversion, and microstructural evolution. Recent scientific advances demonstrate a transition from empirical dissolution testing to mechanistically informed and biopredictive methodologies. Collectively, the available evidence suggests that predictive dissolution testing of LAIs should be formulation-specific and designed to reproduce the dominant release mechanisms under physiologically relevant conditions, thereby supporting formulation development, IVIVC establishment, and regulatory evaluation.

articles.title: 3D printing of medicines: regulatory and quality perspectives.
articles.abstract: Conventional "one-size-fits-all" industrially manufactured medicines often fail to meet the specific therapeutic needs of vulnerable or minoritarian populations, such as the pediatric and geriatric patients. While traditional compounding addresses these gaps, it faces significant quality, scalability, and standardization limitations. Three-dimensional (3D) printing has emerged as a transformative additive manufacturing technology, enabling the precise, layer-by-layer fabrication of personalized oral dosage forms. This review comprehensively analyzes the regulatory landscape, quality requirements, and recent clinical advances of 3D printed pharmaceuticals. At the industrial level, 3D printing demonstrates compatibility with existing Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and conventional regulatory pathways, as evidenced by U.S. Food and Drug Administration -approved and late-stage clinical products. Conversely, decentralized point-of-care manufacturing within hospitals and pharmacies currently lacks a specific, harmonized regulatory framework. However, an increasing number of clinical trials, particularly focusing on dose-sensitive pediatric therapies, and the introduction of novel decentralized regulatory models highlight its clinical viability. In conclusion, while pharmaceutical 3D printing is reaching technological maturation, traditional quality guidelines must be updated to address its unique digital attributes. Collaborative efforts between regulators, academia, and industry are crucial to successfully implement 3D printing into routine personalized healthcare.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-based therapies for obesity-associated metabolic complications: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a major global health challenge and a key driver of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic syndrome. Although pharmacological therapies and bariatric surgery have improved both short- and long-term outcomes, with GLP-1 receptor agonists now demonstrating cardiovascular and heart-failure benefits beyond weight reduction (SELECT, SUMMIT), durable and broadly applicable treatments for all patients remain limited. In this context, mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapies, particularly adipose-derived MSCs, have gained increasing attention due to their immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory properties demonstrated in preclinical models. Experimental studies suggest that MSCs influence adipose tissue remodeling, immune cell polarization, insulin sensitivity, and energy homeostasis predominantly through paracrine mechanisms, including the release of cytokines and extracellular vesicles, rather than long-term engraftment or differentiation. However, accumulating evidence indicates that obesity itself profoundly impairs endogenous MSC function through oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic alterations, raising important concerns regarding the feasibility of autologous MSC-based approaches in obese individuals. Critically, no randomized controlled trial has evaluated MSC therapy for obesity with weight loss, body composition, or obesity-related clinical outcomes as primary endpoints; the available human evidence addresses glycemic control in type 2 diabetes and metabolic complications. In this review, we summarize current mechanistic insights, preclinical findings, and clinical data on MSC-based interventions for obesity-associated metabolic disorders, while critically discussing key biological, manufacturing, and regulatory challenges. Finally, we define the prerequisites for rational translation - standardized potency assays, obesity-specific early-phase trials with active comparators, objective body-composition endpoints, hemocompatibility testing, and long-term surveillance.

articles.title: Targeting protective renin-angiotensin system pathways in pulmonary emphysema: Preclinical evidence for resolving inflammation and restoring lung homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide and still lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. Current pharmacological treatments primarily alleviate symptoms and reduce exacerbations, but have limited ability to prevent progressive lung destruction or promote tissue repair. Increasing evidence indicates that beyond the classical cardiovascular functions of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), it additionally plays a central role in regulating pulmonary inflammation, oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodelling, cellular senescence and endogenous repair mechanisms. Experimental studies have shown that both pharmacological inhibition of the ACE/Ang II/AT1 axis and activation of the protective AT2 receptor and ACE2/Ang-(1-7)/Mas pathways attenuate multiple pathological processes involved in COPD progression. In this review, we comprehensively discuss the current preclinical evidence supporting pharmacological manipulation of the RAS in experimental models of pulmonary emphysema, highlighting the anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-fibrotic, pro-resolutive and regenerative mechanisms associated with these therapeutic strategies. We further discuss emerging evidence indicating that activation of protective RAS pathways not only suppresses inflammation, but also promotes tissue repair through modulating autophagy, inflammasome activation, cellular senescence and endogenous regenerative signalling. These findings collectively position protective RAS modulation as a promising disease-modifying strategy for COPD and provide a strong rationale for future translational and clinical studies aimed at restoring pulmonary homeostasis.

articles.title: Biomaterial-based local drug delivery in autoimmune and immune-mediated inflammatory diseases: An exposure-centric narrative review.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune and immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and psoriasis, often demonstrate incomplete responses to systemic therapies. This limitation may reflect not only insufficient pharmacological potency but also inadequate control of drug exposure at the site of action. While upstream immune activation is frequently systemic, tissue injury is influenced by compartmentalized effector processes, highlighting the importance of spatial and temporal drug distribution within diseased tissues. Biomaterial-based delivery systems, including hydrogels, nanoparticles, lipid carriers, microneedles, and hybrid constructs, are increasingly recognized not only as drug transport vehicles but also as modulators of local exposure. Their therapeutic performance is shaped by disease-specific biological barriers, including synovial compartmentalization in rheumatoid arthritis, mucosal transport limitations in inflammatory bowel disease, and epidermal constraints in psoriasis. Stimuli-responsive systems may further enable context-dependent modulation of drug availability, although their impact on clinically relevant exposure metrics remains insufficiently defined. Unlike many previous reviews that have largely organized biomaterial systems according to carrier type, therapeutic cargo, or delivery platform, this review interprets existing strategies through the lens of local exposure and disease-specific exposure limitations. However, current evidence supporting local exposure optimization remains heterogeneous, ranging from direct pharmacokinetic measurements to imaging-based localization and pharmacodynamic inference. This narrative review provides an exposure-centric perspective by integrating local concentration, tissue distribution, and exposure duration to reinterpret current biomaterial-based strategies in autoimmune and immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. By linking disease-specific exposure constraints with delivery design principles, this perspective supports more rational exposure-informed development of localized immunomodulatory therapies.

articles.title: Once-Weekly Insulin Icodec: A Review of its Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Properties.
articles.abstract: Insulin icodec is a novel long-acting basal insulin engineered for once-weekly administration. Structural modifications enhance reversible albumin binding and slow insulin receptor binding, resulting in protracted exposure and glucose-lowering effect. The clinical pharmacology of icodec was characterised using consistent methodology across populations with type 2 or type 1 diabetes. Icodec has a half-life of approximately 7 days and pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles covering the full weekly dosing interval. It displays dose-proportional exposure, week-to-week predictability, with an intra-individual coefficient of variation in total exposure of 5.9%, and a comparable glucose-lowering effect independent of injection region. Following treatment initiation, icodec clinical steady state is achieved after 3-4 weeks-this can be reduced by 1 week if the first icodec dose is 50% increased. If, unintentionally, a too high insulin dose is administered, hypoglycaemia risk with icodec is comparable to that of daily basal insulin, including robust physiological counter-regulation to hypoglycaemia. During exercise or prolonged fasting, glucose metrics remained within recommended targets, with no clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia, and supplemental glucose, when required, effectively prevented clinically relevant hypoglycaemia. The pharmacological properties of icodec are preserved across patient characteristics, without a clinically relevant impact of age, sex, diabetes type, race, ethnicity, renal or hepatic impairment, serum albumin or anti-insulin icodec antibody level. These findings support predictable, sustained basal insulin coverage suitable for once-weekly administration. This review summarises the evidence on icodec pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties and discusses how these characteristics translate into clinical benefits and specific clinical considerations compared with existing once-daily basal insulin.

articles.title: Cardiovascular outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors across the spectrum of myocardial infarction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) help in heart failure (HF), but their benefit after acute myocardial infarction is unclear. This meta-analysis assesses their impact on mortality and heart failure hospitalization post-acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and identifies which patients benefit most. METHODS: Four databases were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and matched studies comparing SGLT2i with control post-AMI. PRIMARY OUTCOMES: all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF); secondary: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Subgroups and meta-regression examined timing, diabetes, follow-up, design, SGLT2i type and baseline HF/diabetes. RESULTS: Fifteen studies including 117 096 patients (58 613 SGLT2i vs. 58 483 control) were included. A total of 117 096 patients contributed to the all-cause mortality analysis (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.90), whereas 116 992 patients across 14 studies contributed to the HHF analysis (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.88). All-cause mortality was significantly lower in PSM observational studies (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.61-0.67), whereas the reduction did not reach statistical significance in RCTs (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.01), with a significant interaction by study design. HHF reduction occurred with both early and delayed initiation; dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were similarly effective. MACE was significantly lower with SGLT2i, but CV death, recurrent MI and stroke did not differ. Baseline HF or diabetes showed no association with primary outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i reduced HHF after MI, but this benefit should be interpreted cautiously because of small-study effects and possible publication bias. The all-cause mortality benefit is driven by observational studies; RCTs show a favourable but nonsignificant trend.

articles.title: Organic synthesis and antiarthritic effect of 3-hydroxy-1,7-bis (3-nitrophenyl)hepta-1,3,6-trien-5-one against formaldehyde-induced arthritis in mice.
articles.abstract: The present study was designed to evaluate the biochemical and antioxidant properties of a curcumin analog NB5, as well as its effect on trabecular microarchitecture preservation, in a formaldehyde-induced arthritis mouse model. The compound NB5 was synthesized via a condensation reaction of acetylacetone with 3-nitrobenzaldehyde under nitrogen atmosphere, and its structure was confirmed by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HR-MS analyses. Adult male Swiss albino mice (n = 25) were randomly assigned to five groups (n = 5 per group) for in vivo experiments. Additional in vitro assays were conducted using DPPH radical scavenging systems. NB5 was administered orally at doses of 100 and 150 mg/kg for 14 consecutive days following arthritis induction. Diclofenac (10 mg/kg) served as the reference standard, and butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) was used as the positive control for antioxidant assay. In the in vivo experiments, paw edema was measured plethysmographically; blood glucose and serum biochemical parameters (markers of hepatic and renal function) were quantified using standard colorimetric kits. Bone microarchitecture of proximal interphalangeal joint subchondral bone was evaluated using microcomputed tomography (micro-CT), with statistical significance determined using one-way ANOVA followed by appropriate post hoc tests. NB5 exhibited potent DPPH scavenging (IC₅₀ = 9.91 µg/mL), which was superior to that of BHT, as well as this compound, at 100 and 150 mg/kg significantly reduced paw edema, normalized blood glucose, and improved serum biochemistry without hepatorenal toxicity. Micro-CT revealed that NB5 restored trabecular microarchitecture by increasing thickness and number while reducing separation of the bony network; the 150 mg/kg dose demonstrated bone-protective effects comparable to those observed with to diclofenac. NB5 acts as a multifunctional antioxidant and antiarthritic agent with significant preservation of trabecular microarchitecture, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for managing inflammation-associated bone damage without systemic toxicity.

articles.title: TNF/TNFR1 promotes palmitic acid-induced insulin resistance in HepG2 cells by suppressing autophagy-associated signaling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intracellular lipid accumulation is intimately associated with palmitic acid (PA)-induced insulin resistance (IR). This study aimed to clarify the role of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)/tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1) axis in PA-induced IR and lipid metabolic abnormalities in HepG2 cells. METHODS: HepG2 cells were exposed to PA (0-500 μM). Cell injury, glucose metabolism, and lipid accumulation were assessed by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, glucose assay, and Oil Red O staining, respectively. Hub genes were identified from the GSE174475 dataset via differential expression and protein-protein interaction analysis. TNFR1 overexpression and TNF silencing were performed to validate function. Autophagic flux was evaluated by LC3 II/p62 expression, immunofluorescence, transmission electron microscopy, and bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1) treatment. RESULTS: PA (250 μM) impaired insulin signaling, reducing AKT phosphorylation, plasma membrane glucose transporter 2 (GLUT2)/glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4) levels, glucose uptake, and insulin responsiveness. PA increased TNF expression and promoted lipid accumulation via SREBP1c and lipogenesis/lipid uptake. TNF knockdown attenuated PA-induced IR-related alterations, lipid deposition, and autophagy-related alterations, whereas TNFR1 overexpression reversed these effects. Baf-A1-based flux analysis further suggested that PA impaired autophagic flux, which was restored by TNF knockdown and reversed by TNFR1 overexpression. LC3 II and p62 changes further suggested that TNF/TNFR1 signaling may contribute to this impairment. CONCLUSION: TNF may impair autophagic flux and lipid metabolism, thereby contributing to PA-induced lipotoxicity and IR-like phenotypes via TNFR1. These findings provide a rationale for targeting TNF/TNFR1 in the treatment of lipid accumulation-associated IR.

articles.title: Analysis of regulatory review models and approval timelines across selected African medicines regulatory authorities using the OpERA framework (2020-2024).
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization (WHO) developed the Global Benchmarking Tool (GBT) to assess national regulatory systems and support regulatory-system strengthening across regulatory functions. Several African National Medicines Regulatory Authorities (NMRAs) have achieved Maturity Level 3 (ML3). This study aimed to compare regulatory review models for medicines, approval timelines for applications for marketing authorisation of medicines and regulatory practices across four African NMRAs and explore how reported approval timelines and selected practices varied according to WHO maturity-level status. METHOD: The Optimising Efficiency in Regulatory Agencies questionnaire was used in the study. The primary analysis focused on contextual trend analysis of overall approval median timelines for products from 2020 to 2024 for new active substances (NASs), biologicals, vaccines, biosimilars and generic products together with product characteristics. The timelines were summarized using medians, IQRs and sample sizes. Descriptive analyses were conducted across the NMRAs. RESULTS: Approval timelines varied substantially across agencies and product categories. The review of median approval timelines for NASs in 2024 demonstrated that Ghana FDA reported the shortest median approval timelines of 70 calendar days (IQR 25 to 120, n = 30); followed by MCAZ with 603 calendar days (n = 3) then SAHPRA with 628 calendar days (IQR 416 to 937, n = 12) and ZAMRA reported 1242 calendar days (n = 3). CONCLUSION: From this study, it was observed that Ghana FDA has shorter median approval timelines throughout the period under review as compared with the other NMRAs. The findings suggest that evaluation of regulatory processes may assist NMRAs in identifying operational practices associated with improved efficiency.

articles.title: Nuclear BCL10 translocation contributes to lymphoma progression and poor prognosis of peripheral T-cell lymphomas.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: We evaluated the clinical and biological significance of nuclear BCL10 localization and related signaling in peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCLs). METHODS: We examined the expression of signaling molecules linked to apoptosis, and AKT/BCL10/BCL3/NF-κB-related signaling molecules in both T-cell lymphoma (TCL) cell lines (SR786 and HuT78). Two TCL cells treated with or without siBCL10 transfection were injected into the mice's flanks in order to evaluate the anti-tumor efficacy of BCL10 knockdown in the xenograft model. We assessed the expression patterns of phosphorylated (p)-AKT/BCL10/BCL3/NF-κB (p65) in tumor cells in 95 patients with PTCLs using immunohistochemical staining. RESULTS: In both TCL cell lines, siBCL10 inhibited cell viability, arrested cell cycles in the sub-G1 phase, and enhanced the cytotoxicity of doxorubicin and gemcitabine. The siBCL10 upregulated the expression of cleaved PARP, downregulated the expression of nuclear BCL3, NF-κB, and MYC, and reduced the transcriptional activity of NF-κB and NF-κB signaling-related molecules in both TCL cell lines. In both TCL cell lines-derived xenograft mouse models, siBCL10 attenuated tumor growth in TCLs. Patients expressing p-AKT (p = 0.025), nuclear BCL10 (p = 0.001), nuclear BCL3 (p = 0.010), or nuclear NF-κB (p = 0.010) had shorter 5-year overall survival (OS) rates than those not expressing them, respectively. Genetic alterations in T-cell receptor-signaling pathways were more often found in patients with nuclear BCL10 expression. Patients with both nuclear BCL10 expression and RHOA mutation had a significantly worse OS than those without either expression or mutation (p = 0.008). CONCLUSION: Nuclear BCL10 translocation contributes to lymphoma progression and poor prognosis in PTCLs by activating NF-κB signaling.

articles.title: The Matrikine Proline-Glycine-Proline Links Neutrophilic Inflammation and Tissue Remodeling in Colorectal Cancer.
articles.abstract: Chronic inflammation and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation are key features of carcinogenesis and tumor progression. We investigated the expression of proline-glycine-proline (PGP), an ECM-derived neutrophilic chemoattractant, in both tumor and serum samples from colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. We also correlated PGP levels with pathological and clinical outcomes. Our study included 88 previously untreated CRC patients who underwent surgical resection. Notably, PGP levels were significantly elevated in tumors compared to adjacent normal tissue, alongside neutrophilic infiltration. We explored enzymatic pathways critical to PGP persistence in the tumor microenvironment, observing increased expression of PGP-generating proteases like prolyl endopeptidase (PE) and MMP-9, and reduced PGP breakdown via LTA4H. The complementary peptide, l-arginine-threonine-arginine (RTR), impedes PGP-high expressed tumor lysates-induced chemotaxis in vitro. Elevated tumor PGP was associated with decreased disease-free survival (p=0.0235), and serum PGP levels correlated with tumor T stage. Additionally, we found a positive correlation between tumor-related cytokines in the serum and PGP expression. These findings demonstrate that PGP is associated with inflammatory and clinical features of CRC and support further investigation into its biological and clinical significance.

articles.title: The anti-fibrotic and anti-proliferative effects of pirfenidone in androgen-induced prostate growth: involvement of the regulation of HDAC expression, EMT and TGF-β1/Smad2/3 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) involves progressive prostate enlargement and fibrosis. Pirfenidone exerts anti-fibrotic effects by downregulating transforming growth factor beta1 (TGF-β1) expression. The role of histone deacetylase (HDAC), TGF-β1 and the therapeutic effects of pirfenidone in the treatment of BPH remain unclear. Pirfenidone orally attenuated prostate growth in ICR mice (n= 12/group) induced by the subcutaneous injection of 7.5 mg/kg testosterone propionate (TP) for 28 days. The inhibition rate of prostate index (prostate/body weight ratio) was 33.10% and 55.83% in pirfenidone (500, 750 mg/kg) treatment groups compared with the TP-treated group. Treatment with pirfenidone downregulated the expression of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and fibrosis-associated proteins, including TGF-β1, p-Smad, α-SMA, collagen I, collagen III, collagen IV, N-cadherin, vimentin, and fibronectin. Pirfenidone (750 mg/kg) inhibited the protein expression of class I HDACs (68%-95% reduction) compared with the TP-treated group. Additionally, pirfenidone inhibited inflammation by downregulating NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome formation. After treatment with pirfenidone (5000 μM) for 72 h, the cell survival rate was 55.40% and 52.98% in benign prostatic hyperplasia epithelial cell (BPH-1) and prostate stromal cell (WPMY-1). After 72 h, pirfenidone (5000 μM) inhibited the expression of class I HDACs and cell growth in BPH-1 and WPMY-1 cells with or without TGF-β1 treatment. The anti-proliferative and anti-fibrotic effects of pirfenidone were accompanied by the attenuation of TGF-β1-mediated signaling pathway, along with the modulation of EMT, HDAC expression, and inflammatory responses in the prostate. Pirfenidone was identified as a potential alternative medication for preventing the development of BPH.

articles.title: Beyond Acid Suppression: Vonoprazan as a Multi-Target Modulator in Experimental Colitis from Oxidative Stress to Mitochondrial Rescue.
articles.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC); as one of the inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), arises from chronic inflammation of the intestinal tract. In this study, we addressed the possible protective mechanisms of vonoprazan, as a potassium-competitive acid blocker, on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-mediated UC. Therefore, male BALB-c mice administered oral vonoprazan (10 or 20 mg/kg/day) for 10 days and received drinking water containing 3% w/v DSS for 7 days from day 4. Vonoprazan exhibited a promising effect against UC by increasing mice body weight, colon length, and spleen weight, decreasing serum C-reactive protein (CRP) concentration and the disease activity index (DAI), and alleviating colonic histopathological changes. Colonic tissue antioxidants increased significantly in vonoprazan-treated groups. Additionally, colonic tissue oxidative stress was significantly ameliorated in vonoprazan-treated mice. Furthermore, vonoprazan preserved the integrity of intestinal mucosal barrier function and attenuated UC by decreasing the levels of immuno-inflammatory cells, inflammation-related proteins, and pro-inflammatory cytokines, elevating the tight junction proteins levels, and ameliorating mitochondrial energy metabolism. Taken together, vonoprazan protected against DSS-mediated UC in mice via antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities that maintained tight junction architecture.

articles.title: Activation of PDZ-Binding Kinase Contributes to Airway Remodeling in Asthma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Airway remodeling is an important pathological feature of refractory asthma. PDZ-binding kinase (PBK), as a serine/threonine protein kinase, has been extensively studied in various biological processes. However, the role of PBK in airway smooth muscle cells (ASMCs) proliferation and airway remodeling remains unclear. In addition, sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) has been proven to play a key role in the progression of airway remodeling. The present study aims to investigate whether PBK mediates S1P-induced ASMCs proliferation and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: Ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthmatic rats and primary cultured ASMCs were employed in the study. Inflammatory factor production, airway resistance assessment, histological staining and immunohistochemical staining were conducted to evaluate the development of asthma. CCK-8 and EdU assays were used for the measurement of cell proliferation. Western blotting and Ubiquitination assay were used to detect protein expressions. RESULTS: PBK was up-regulated in lungs of OVA-induced chronic asthmatic rats and mediated airway remodeling. Targeting PBK could alleviate airway wall thickness and ASMCs hyperplasia in asthma model. In cultured ASMCs, S1P reduced ubiquitin-mediated degradation of PBK by down-regulating STUB1 leading to PBK protein accumulation. Meanwhile, S1P induced PBK phosphorylation and activation, which further led to the activation of protein regulator of cytokinesis 1 (PRC1) by increasing its expression and phosphorylation, finally promoting ASMCs proliferation. CONCLUSIONS: Activation of PBK contributes to ASMCs proliferation and airway remodeling in the development of asthma. S1P upregulates PBK expression by suppressing STUB1-mediated proteasome-degradation and elevates PBK activity through increasing its phosphorylation. Activation of PBK further stimulates PRC1 expression and phosphorylation leading to ASMCs proliferation. Targeting PBK might be an effective therapeutic strategy for asthma.

articles.title: Cryptococcus neoformans GXM Mimotopes: Bioactivity and Modulation of Human Inflammatory Response and Oxidative Burst in vitro.
articles.abstract: Beyond their diagnostic potential, mimotopes of the Cryptococcus neoformans glucuronoxylomannan (GXM) capsule may act as potent immunomodulators. This study investigated the biological effects of three GXM-mimetic peptides: linear peptide (PL), cyclic (PC), and double-cyclic peptide (PD) on the activation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and granulocytes. Our results reveal a distinct structure-function relationship in immune signaling. The PD variant significantly enhanced the oxidative burst in granulocytes stimulated by phorbol ester, whereas the PL variant inhibited reactive oxygen species (ROS) production under zymosan-opsonized stimulus. Cytokine profiling showed that PL effectively reduced IL-12p40 levels, mimicking the immunosuppressive nature of native GXM. Conversely, PC and PD variants triggered a pro-inflammatory shift, significantly increasing the secretion of IL-1β and the chemokine CXCL8. Metabolic activity assays confirmed that all mimotopes lacked intrinsic cytotoxicity, maintaining PBMC viability above 98%. These findings demonstrate that GXM-mimetic peptides can either replicate the fungus's immune evasion mechanisms or actively stimulate host defense pathways depending on their conformational state. By transforming fungal evasion motifs into "danger signals," structural stabilization through cyclization provides a molecular switch to bypass the immunological paralysis typically induced by GXM. Such bioactivity positions these peptides as chemically defined candidates for future developing of novel antifungal vaccines and next-generation immunotherapeutic strategies against cryptococcosis.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rh2 Attenuates Post-Myocardial Infarction Heart Failure by Modulating the TGF-β/Smad2 Signaling Pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocardial fibrosis and oxidative stress are key drivers of post-myocardial infarction heart failure (post-MI HF). Ginsenoside Rh2 (GRh2) has shown cardioprotective potential, but its role in post-MI HF and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. METHODS: Mice with permanent left anterior descending artery ligation were treated with GRh2 (10 mg/kg/day, gavage) or enalapril for 28 days, cardiac function (echocardiography), fibrosis (histology/immunohistochemistry) and cardiac injury markers were assessed. Cardiac transcriptomes were sequenced to identify enriched pathways. H9C2 cardiomyoblasts and human iPSC-derived cardiac organoids were subjected to oxygen glucose deprivation (OGD) and treated with GRh2 with or without the TGF-β receptor agonist SRI-011381 (SRI), viability, oxidative stress, apoptosis, fibrosis and TGF-β/Smad2 signalling were measured. RESULTS: In vivo, GRh2 treatment markedly improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial fibrosis in mice with post-MI heart failure. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the TGF-β signaling pathway was substantially enriched. In vitro, GRh2 treatment significantly improved cell viability and reduced oxidative stress and fibrosis in OGD-exposed H9C2 cardiomyocytes and cardiac organoids. These protective effects were strongly associated with the suppression of the TGF-β/Smad2 signaling pathway. CONCLUSIONS: GRh2 can improve myocardial function and alleviate fibrosis, oxidative stress and cell apoptosis after MI. In cells and organoids, these protective effects depend on the inhibition of the TGF-β/Smad2 signaling pathway, suggesting that this pathway is a potential mediator of the cardiac protective effect of GRh2.

articles.title: Mechanisms underlying the effects of Buyang Huanwu Decoction against sepsis-induced ARDS using network pharmacology and experimental validation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHW), a classic formula from Yilin Gaicuo Qing Dynasty, is indicated for stroke in patients with qi deficiency and blood stasis in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with qi deficiency, blood stasis, and heat-toxin obstructing the lungs, which align with the therapeutic actions of this formula. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the effects of BYHW on sepsis-induced ARDS and the mechanisms underlying these effects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ARDS was induced through LPS treatment in wild-type and eNOS-deficient (eNOS-/-) mice. The components of BYHW were analyzed using UPLC-UV-MS. Potential associated targets and pathways were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking experiments. Relevant protein and mRNA expression levels were assessed by Western blot analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, or qPCR. RESULTS: BYHW significantly improving the hypothermia, elevated plasma levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, the lung index and injury induced by LPS in wild-type (WT) mice. However, these effects of BYHW were markedly in eNOS-/- mice. LPS downregulated AQP1 protein expression and upregulated Cav-1 protein expression and the p-P65/P65 ratio in both groups but increased the p-IκB/IκB ratio only in the WT mice. Pretreatment of BYHW increased the expression of eNOS and AQP1, decreased the Cav-1 expression and P65/IκB phosphorylation in WT mice, but the action on the P65/IκB phosphorylation and AQP1 expression were abrogated in eNOS-/- mice. CONCLUSION: BYHW protect against sepsis-induced ARDS may be related to decrease the eNOS-NF-κB-mediated synthesis of inflammatory cytokines and upregulation of AQP1 expression.

articles.title: Genetic GHSR deficiency and LEAP2 treatment enhance the glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide in male mice in a metabolic state-dependent manner.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Liraglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist that lowers glycemia and is used to treat type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. Activation of the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) increases glycemia. We aimed to determine whether GHSR inhibition enhances the glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We investigated the acute glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide in mice with genetic GHSR deletion or pharmacological GHSR blockade under fed, fasting, and postprandial conditions. We also examined the potential cellular basis of this interaction in murine islets using transcriptomic and immunolabeling approaches and in human pancreatic tissue using a publicly available transcriptomic dataset. KEY FINDINGS: Liraglutide similarly reduced glycemia in ad libitum-fed GHSR-null and control mice. Following food deprivation, liraglutide more effectively attenuated postprandial increases in glycemia in male, but not female, GHSR-null mice than in control mice. Liraglutide reduced glycemia in fasted GHSR-null male mice but not in WT males. In male mice, pretreatment with a LEAP2 (liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide 2) analog, an endogenous GHSR antagonist and inverse agonist, enhanced the glucose-lowering effects of liraglutide under postprandial and fasting conditions. GHSR and GLP-1R showed limited co-expression in murine islets. In human islets, their co-expression was also limited and enriched in δ-cells, but was also detected in β-cells, where the proportion of GHSR+/GLP-1R+ cells was higher in donors with T2D. SIGNIFICANCE: GHSR inhibition enhances liraglutide's glucose-lowering effects in a sex-dependent manner, highlighting GHSR as a potential target to improve GLP-1R agonist efficacy.

articles.title: Glycosylated steroidal saponins suppress HNSCC progression by targeting the RAS-ERK pathway.
articles.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by high incidence, pronounced invasiveness and metastasis, and poor prognosis, underscoring an urgent need for novel and effective therapeutic strategies. Natural steroidal saponins serve as promising anti-tumor leads, yet prior work only reports their downstream ERK suppression, lacking upstream regulators and systematic glycosylation-related structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis. This study focused on diosgenin and its two glycosylated derivatives. Firstly, in vitro cell proliferation, apoptosis and invasion assays combined with an in vivo subcutaneous xenograft model were performed to verify anti-HNSCC activities of the candidate compounds. Subsequently, core genes were screened via network pharmacology and machine learning, and validated by molecular docking, pull-down and Western blotting. All three compounds exhibit significant anti-HNSCC activity in vitro and vivo, which increases progressively with the number of glycosyl groups. Combined network pharmacology and machine learning analyses screened out 11 core genes, based on which a stable diagnostic prediction model was constructed. Molecular docking verified that the three saponins can stably bind to and suppress EPHB4 and ADAM17. The Raf1-RBD pull-down assay further confirmed that these saponins markedly reduce the level of intracellular active RAS and specifically downregulate ERK phosphorylation, ultimately restraining the malignant progression of HNSCC. This work reveals the RAS-MAPK inhibitory axis by targeting EPHB4 and ADAM17 of glycosylated steroidal saponins for the first time and highlights glycosylation as a critical activity-boosting moiety, supporting RAS-targeted lead discovery and structural optimisation against HNSCC.

articles.title: Machine learning-based stability optimization design and virtual screening of the anti-pulmonary fibrosis peptide DR3penA.
articles.abstract: The novel anti-fibrotic peptide DR3penA, previously developed by our research group, demonstrates substantial therapeutic potential; however, its inherent limited metabolic stability in vivo, attributable to its linear structure, hinders clinical translation. Although cyclization represents a key strategy for enhancing peptide structural rigidity, exhaustive trial-and-error exploration across the vast chemical modification space entails prohibitive computational and experimental costs. In this study, we constructed a machine learning-assisted virtual screening framework for the rational optimization of peptide stability and bioactivity. This framework integrates a stability prediction model with an ensemble bioactivity prediction model based on XGBoost and LightGBM, and employs comprehensive scoring alongside Pareto front analysis to perform multi-objective screening of candidate analogs. Computational evaluation showed that, under leakage-audited cluster splitting, the stability XGBoost model exhibits strong ranking capability (test Spearman ρ = 0.751; NDCG@10 = 0.969), and the XGBoost-LightGBM ensemble achieves high predictive performance for a pan-peptide bioactivity proxy (test R² = 0.822). A virtual library of 95 analogues was generated by predefined chemical rules; cyclization sites were enumerated rather than discovered de novo, and the models were used to rank these schemes. Three analogues (DR3penA_001, _011, and _076) were nominated as a representative panel covering distinct cyclization chemistries, rather than the three highest composite scores. Altogether, this hierarchical, leakage-aware framework enables stability-prioritized, multi-objective nomination of DR3penA analogues and provides a transferable, data-driven strategy for peptide redesign.

articles.title: TREM2/IGF-1 Signaling Axis-induced microglial senescence Underlies Benzo[a]pyrene-associated Parkinson's Disease-like Lesions.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. Accumulating evidence has linked environmental polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), with benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P) as a representative ubiquitous member, to elevated PD risk and disease pathogenesis. The present study aimed to investigate whether B[a]P can trigger typical PD-like lesions in mice, and further dissects the functional role of microglial senescence as well as its underlying regulatory mechanism, using complementary systems in vivo mouse model and in vitro BV2 microglia cell. Behavioral assessments revealed that B[a]P exposure induced significant, dose-dependent impairments in motor coordination and cognitive function compared with the control group. Moreover, the degree of functional impairments measured in the high-dose B[a]P group was comparable to that observed in the MPTP positive-control group. Following B[a]P treatment, brain-resident microglia cells exhibited signs of cell senescence, as evidenced by typical ultrastructural alterations, increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) activity, and elevated expression of the core senescence markers p16, p21, and p53 proteins. Consistent with these in vivo observations, B[a]P was confirmed to also induce cell cycle arrest in cultured BV2 microglia cells. This pro-senescent effect was significnatly attenuated by Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) overexpression, whereas it was markedly exacerbated following TREM2 knockout. Subsequent experiments further validated that insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), as a direct downstream effector regulated by TREM2, is functionally required for B[a]P-triggered microglial senescence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that B[a]P exposure can induce PD-like lesions and microglial senescence, and which is primarily mediated via the TREM2/IGF-1 signaling axis.

articles.title: Arsenic promotes MIN6 cells dysfunction via ACO2-αKG-mitophagy pathway.
articles.abstract: Arsenite can impair pancreatic β-cell function, but the mechanisms linking mitochondrial metabolic disturbances to this toxicity remain incompletely understood. Therefore, mitophagy, which removes dysfunctional mitochondria by lysosomal degradation, has attracted much attention. Mitochondrial (cis)aconitase 2 (ACO2) is a critical enzyme in the tricarboxylic acid cycle responsible for coordinating mitochondrial functions and is involved in energy metabolism. However, the role of ACO2 in arsenite-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and altered mitophagy in pancreatic β cells remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that arsenic exposure leads to the downregulation of mitochondrial ACO2. As expected, ACO2 overexpression reversed the arsenic-induced MIN6 cells dysfunction. In addition, arsenic induced the inhibition of mitophagy in islets β-cells characteristic with the downregulation of PTEN-induced putative kinase 1 (PINK1) , Parkin RBR E3 ubiquitin protein ligase (Parkin) and sequestosome 1 (p62/SQSTM1), accompanied by an increased level of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3-II (LC3-II). ACO2 reversed these alterations in protein expression. Simultaneously, ACO2 overexpression elevated adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) levels, decreased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) production, and alleviated the functional impairment of β-cells induced by arsenic. Moreover, supplementation with α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), a downstream metabolite of ACO2, similarly mitigated arsenic-induced mitophagy inhibition and functional impairment of MIN6 cells. In conclusion, this study identified a novel mechanism by which inorganic arsenic can lead to pancreatic β cell dysfunction via the ACO2-αKG-mitophagy pathway. These findings advance the mechanistic understanding of arsenite-induced β-cell toxicity.

articles.title: Parthenolide reduces transgelin-2 expression in inhibiting glioblastoma malignancy through activating GSK3β-suppressing CREB signaling.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a WHO grade IV brain tumor with aggressive growth and frequent recurrence, and temozolomide (TMZ) remains the standard first-line chemotherapy despite limited durable benefits. Parthenolide (Pt), a sesquiterpene lactone derived from the medicinal plant feverfew, has shown antitumor activity in multiple cancer types; however, its therapeutic potential and downstream mechanisms in GBM have not been fully defined. Herein, we demonstrate that Pt induces apoptosis, suppresses stemness, and reduces invasion in human U-87MG and T98G cells. Pt also potentiates TMZ's efficacy in vitro and in an orthotopic GBM model with male NOD-SCID mice. RNA-sequencing and pathway analyses revealed that Pt markedly represses epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated programs. Among the most significantly downregulated genes, transgelin-2 (TAGLN2) emerged as a key Pt-responsive target, and its high expression was correlated with poor survival in glioma cohorts. TAGLN2 overexpression rescued Pt-mediated suppression of malignant phenotypes and the EMT, supporting a functional role for TAGLN2 in Pt responsiveness. Mechanistically, inhibitor screening identified glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β) as a critical upstream regulator of Pt-induced TAGLN2 repression. Promoter-reporter and ChIP-qPCR assays further showed that Pt activates GSK3β, leading to reduced cyclic AMP response-binding protein (CREB) transcriptional activity and diminished CREB occupancy at the TAGLN2 promoter, thereby suppressing TAGLN2 transcription. Collectively, our findings define a Pt-driven GSK3β/CREB/TAGLN2 axis that restrains the mesenchymal transition and enhances TMZ sensitivity in GBM, highlighting TAGLN2 and its upstream regulatory pathway as potential therapeutic targets for this lethal disease.

articles.title: Chemogenetic Manipulation of the Cortical Amygdala Alters Binge-Like Alcohol Drinking in Male mice and Neural Network Function in Male and Female Mice.
articles.abstract: Binge drinking is a prevalent and clinically significant behavior contributing to alcohol use disorder. Sex differences in binge drinking are observed in both humans and preclinical studies, including differences in alcohol intake and underlying neural regulatory mechanisms. The cortical amygdala (CoA) has been implicated in alcohol-related behaviors, but its role in binge-like drinking and associated brain-wide co-activation patterns remains unclear. We tested whether CoA activity regulates binge-like alcohol consumption in a sex-dependent manner and examined CoA-associated brain-wide network organization in binge-like drinking. Binge-like alcohol intake was assessed using a 6-week Drinking-in-the-Dark paradigm. Saline or deschloroclozapine was administered 30 min before drinking in mice with inhibitory hM4Di, excitatory hM3Dq, or mCherry control virus. Locomotor and anxiety-like behavior were assessed 24 h after the final 4-h DID session. Brains were collected 120 min after drinking onset during a final DID session under chemogenetic manipulation. Whole-brain Fos mapping was performed, and brain-wide co-activation networks were constructed, followed by graph theory analyses. CoA inhibition significantly reduced binge-like alcohol consumption in male mice, but not females, although the drug × sex × virus interaction was not significant. CoA activation did not alter alcohol intake in either sex but increased locomotor activity in females but not males, although the corresponding sex interaction was not significant. Anxiety-like behavior was unaffected. CoA inhibition was associated with distinct brain-wide network configurations, including differences in CoA-associated module composition, hub-like node distribution, and co-activation patterns involving alcohol-relevant limbic and hypothalamic regions. These findings support a sex-dependent pattern of CoA regulation of binge-like drinking, with the reduction in alcohol intake detected in males but not females and demonstrate that CoA activity shapes brain-wide Fos co-activation patterns during alcohol consumption.

articles.title: Adolescent social isolation drives sex-dependent shifts in medial prefrontal cortex endocannabinoid tone and excitatory/inhibitory balance: the protective role of a methyl donor.
articles.abstract: Prolonged social isolation triggers neuropsychiatric impairments linked to brain neurotransmitter imbalances. This study investigated the impact of social isolation on sensory perception, affective states, and the levels of amino acid neurotransmitters and endocannabinoids within the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of both male and female adolescent mice. Furthermore, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), a methyl donor with established antidepressant properties, mitigating these alterations. Single-housed (SH) male mice developed mechanical allodynia, cold hyperalgesia, depression-like behavior, and general malaise, alongside significantly decreased GABA levels in the mPFC. SAMe treatment effectively ameliorated these symptoms, restoring GABAergic tone and increasing glycine and glutamate levels. In contrast, SH female mice exhibited anxiety-like behavior and pain hypersensitivity without depression-like traits. Their neurochemical profile was characterized by decreased GABA but increased levels of glutamate and specific endocannabinoids/acylethanolamides (2-AG, PEA, and LEA) in the mPFC. In females, SAMe treatment successfully reversed anxiety-like behaviors and pain hypersensitivity, normalized glutamate, LEA, and GABA levels, and increased glycine and DHG. Our findings demonstrate that while social isolation-induced neuropsychiatric and neurochemical alterations are sex-dependent, the development of sensory hypersensitivity and the therapeutic responsiveness to SAMe are consistent across sexes. By restoring GABAergic homeostasis and modulating excitatory and endocannabinoid signaling in the mPFC, SAMe emerges as a promising pharmacological intervention for treating the complex psychiatric and sensory sequelae induced by chronic social stress.

articles.title: Microstructure-driven opacity of semi-permeable membranes in push-pull osmotic tablets and its impact on manufacturability and drug release.
articles.abstract: Push-pull osmotic pump tablets provide controlled, zero-order drug release through water diffusion across a semi-permeable membrane and extrusion of the drug in the active layer through a laser-drilled orifice. The membranes must be mechanically robust to channel the internal osmotic pressure towards drug extrusion. The study reports an instance in which the solvent coating produced opaque cellulose acetate/PEG3350 semi-permeable membranes. This reduced the visual contrast between the push and pull layers-creating a potential risk for accurate laser drilling-and led to incomplete dissolution of investigational drug MK-8189 after 24 h. Scanning electron microscopy, light microscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, nanoindentation, x-ray micro-computed tomography, and dissolution testing were used to identify the origin and impact of the opacity. Results showed that opacity was driven by coating-induced membrane porosity, rather than phase separation. Although both presentations retained the zero-order release kinetics, the opaque membranes were more porous and mechanically weaker-exhibiting a three-fold increase in the number of pores, a statistically significant increase in pore size distribution, and a 26% reduction Young's Modulus than the transparent membranes. During dissolution, the softer opaque membranes deformed substantially, increasing internal tablet volume and reducing the fraction of swelling capacity available to drive the drug extrusion. Consequently, opaque tablets plateaued at ∼85% drug release, whereas transparent tablets achieved complete release. By understanding the edges of failure for the solvent coating process, optimization of the air-to-spray ratio, product temperature, and pattern air pressure eliminated the microstructural porosity.

articles.title: Disulfide bond-modified ionizable lipids for co-delivery of siRNA and carbon dots in the treatment of acute liver injury.
articles.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe clinical condition characterized by excessive oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, for which effective targeted therapeutic strategies remain limited. In this study, a redox-responsive ionizable lipid (Lipid S) was designed by incorporating a disulfide bond into its hydrophobic tail. Under reductive conditions, cleavage of the disulfide bond triggered rapid disassembly of the lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), enabling controlled cargo release.
