Using Lipid S, a nanoplatform (CD-siL@LNP-S) was established by loading small interfering RNA against interleukin-11 receptor alpha-1 (siIL11ra1) onto carbon dots (CDs) and encapsulating the resulting complex within lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). CD-siL@LNP-S exhibited stable physicochemical properties, efficiently silenced IL11ra1 expression, and reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production without inducing cytotoxicity. In an acetaminophen-induced ALI mouse model, the formulation preferentially accumulated in the liver and was efficiently taken up by hepatocytes, resulting in significant attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and tissue injury while maintaining good systemic safety. Overall, Lipid S provides a simple and effective strategy for redox-responsive nucleic acid delivery, and CD-siL@LNP-S represents a promising therapeutic approach for oxidative stress-related liver diseases and other conditions with reductive intracellular environments.

articles.title: Enhancing mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine-induced T cell responses by simple supplementation with class B CpG oligodeoxynucleotides.
articles.abstract: mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines can elicit robust T cell responses; however, these responses remain insufficient, particularly in the context of cancer vaccine therapy. Although several types of adjuvants reportedly enhance T cell responses induced by mRNA-LNP vaccines, few comprehensive side-by-side comparisons exist, and it remains unclear which adjuvants are most suitable. Herein, we screened 15 adjuvants. The addition of class B CpG oligodeoxynucleotides (ODNs) markedly augmented T cell induction in an interleukin-12-dependent manner and promoted the antitumor effects of mRNA-LNP vaccines in mice. Class B CpG ODN-adjuvanted mRNA-LNP vaccines induced more potent T cell responses than the mRNA-LNP vaccine administered at a 10-fold higher dose, while exhibiting a more favorable safety profile. However, this approach also reduced the cellular uptake of mRNA-LNPs and antigen expression. As a possible mechanism underlying this reduced delivery efficiency, we found that class B CpG ODNs adsorbed onto LNPs and altered their particle characteristics. These findings demonstrate that supplementation with class B CpG ODN is a simple, safe, and readily implementable approach for enhancing mRNA-LNP vaccine-induced T cell responses. This study also highlights that adding auxiliary components to mRNA-LNPs can potentially affect the performance of LNPs as delivery carriers.

articles.title: Engineered prototypes of Rotahaler® for mechanistic optimization of internal geometry for enhanced dry powder aerosolization: a combined approach of in silico CFD-DPM modeling and stereolithographic 3D printing.
articles.abstract: The Rotahaler®, a widely used commercial capsule-based dry powder inhaler (DPI), is limited by suboptimal lung deposition which is attributed to weak turbulence generation and incomplete deagglomeration of the drug powder. A systematic, device-focused redesign of its geometry is therefore needed to improve aerosolization. This study evaluated the effect of modified device geometries and the resulting airflow resistance on aerosol performance. The approach combined in silico computational fluid dynamics with the discrete particle model (CFD-DPM) and stereolithographic (SLA) 3D printing. The engineered prototypes were then characterized in vitro for aerodynamic particle size distribution (APSD) using an Andersen cascade impactor (ACI). CFD-predicted airflow resistance agreed closely with experimental measurements across all five device geometries (0.46-4.07 % relative error) validating the continuous-phase flow model. The CFD simulations predicted that the engineered impaction regions generated stable vortical flow and increased local turbulence. These flow features were consistent with the improved aerosolization measured experimentally. The APSD analysis of baseline Rotahaler® and final prototype resulted increased fine particle fraction (FPF) from 18.25 % to 29.68 %. Further, reduced mass median aerodynamic diameter (MMAD) from 5.15 ± 0.08 µm to 4.46 ± 0.09 µm and geometric standard deviation (GSD) from 2.71 ± 0.09 to 1.41 ± 0.08 indicated enhanced respirable fraction than the commercial baseline device. CFD-DPM indicated that the combined design of prototype 4 increased capsule chamber turbulence and mouthpiece fluidization expecting to favour powder deagglomeration. Overall, CFD-guided redesign combined with 3D printing offers a proof of concept for optimizing internal geometry of DPI.

articles.title: Machine learning-guided chondrocyte membrane-camouflaged lipid nanoparticles for intra-articular SOX9 mRNA therapy of osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) progression involves cartilage matrix loss and persistent inflammation. This study developed a machine learning-guided and chondrocyte membrane-camouflaged lipid nanoparticle carrying messenger RNA (CM-LNP@mRNA) platform for intra-articular SOX9 delivery. Random forest analysis identified the nitrogen-to-phosphorus and SM-102 ratios as primary determinants with feature importance values of 0.57 and 0.32 respectively. Following ML-guided formulation selection and experimental membrane-coating optimization, the final CM-LNP@mRNA formulation showed an encapsulation efficiency of 95.50% and a particle size of 133.70 nm. Compared with the conventional reference formulation prepared under the same final coating condition, encapsulation efficiency increased from 89.20% to 95.50% and particle size decreased from 145.40 nm to 133.70 nm. Membrane coating shifted the zeta potential from -25.57 mV to -35.07 mV. This transition provided biophysical evidence of successful surface modification. In interleukin-1β-stimulated chondrocytes, CM-LNP@mRNA increased the relative expression of Col2a1 and Acan from 0.20 to 0.33 and from 0.50 to 0.73, respectively, while reducing the relative expression of Mmp3 and Adamts5 from 10.50 to 7.80 and from 4.00 to 2.50, respectively. These alterations indicated a shift toward a matrix-preserving transcriptional state. Downstream matrix metalloproteinase 3 and prostaglandin E2 concentrations decreased from 37.10 ng/mL to 18.50 ng/mL and from 113.70 pg/mL to 76.50 pg/mL by day 7. This reduction demonstrated effective suppression of catabolic and inflammatory activity. In OA rats, CM-LNP@mRNA reduced the osteophyte volume from 4.00 mm3 to 2.00 mm3 and prolonged the thermal response latency from 7.50 s to 11.80 s. These improvements linked cellular metabolic regulation to functional joint recovery. These findings establish a strategy integrating formulation optimization with biomimetic membrane coating to modulate the OA microenvironment.

articles.title: Real-time characterization of ibuprofen-loaded matrix tablets using CMOS-based UV-Vis imaging: influence of sodium bicarbonate-citric acid effervescent system on drug release and matrix behavior.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the applicability of CMOS-based dual-wavelength UV-Vis imaging for real-time characterization of ibuprofen-loaded HPMC K15M matrix tablets containing a sodium bicarbonate-anhydrous citric acid effervescent system. The effervescent system was incorporated at 5% and 10% (w/w). Real-time UV-Vis imaging was used to simultaneously monitor matrix behavior at 520 nm and IBU release at 255 nm in phosphate buffer (pH 6.8) with and without prior exposure to 0.1 N HCl (pH 1.2) to simulate gastric-to-intestinal pH transition. In phosphate buffer alone, incorporation of the effervescent system promoted water uptake, gel-layer formation, and tablet swelling through CO2 generation, resulting in enhanced IBU release. The effect was most pronounced for 10E10HP tablets, which exhibited approximately 40% tablet expansion and nearly 60% IBU release after 6 h. After prior exposure to HCl, however, the same formulation showed a lower IBU release of approximately 18%, indicating that the initial dissolution environment influenced subsequent matrix transformation and drug release behavior. Real-time UV-Vis imaging enabled visualization of formulation-dependent hydration, gel-layer formation, swelling, and erosion behavior, providing mechanistic insight into effervescent-mediated modification of HPMC matrix performance. This approach may support future optimization of controlled-release matrix formulations by linking formulation composition with matrix behavior and drug release characteristics.

articles.title: Streamlined development of continuous blending through integrated process understanding and predictive modeling.
articles.abstract: Within the framework of continuous manufacturing of drug products, continuous blending plays a central role in the quality of the final product. However, the interplay between material properties and process parameters remains complex and system-dependent. This work presents an integrated experimental and predictive framework to characterize and optimize blending performance in a 70-mm GEA linear continuous blender. A full factorial design study was conducted using different raw materials and blend mixtures covering a wide range of powder properties such as flowability, cohesion, and density. The main goal was to quantify how blender speed, throughput, and blender configuration influence hold-up mass (HUM), mean residence time (MRT), number of blade passes (NBP), and time to reach steady state. Distinct blending regimes were identified, with materials exhibiting shear- or transport-dominated behavior depending on their properties and process conditions. A partial least squares (PLS) model was then created to predict HUM from material attributes and process conditions, enabling the estimation of MRT and NBP profiles for new formulations, with only two material characterization tests: bulk/tapped density and shear cell yield locus. Finally, tablet content uniformity studies and residence time distribution studies showed that higher mixing element configurations and adequate hold-up mass are crucial for effective macromixing and reducing throughput variability from the feeders, especially for low-dose formulations.

articles.title: Accelerative effects of a polyphenolic emulsion hydrogel containing gallic, tannic, and chlorogenic acids on full-thickness excisional wound healing in a murine model.
articles.abstract: Effective healing of acute incisional wounds is essential to improve skin integrity and prevent complications. Natural polyphenols have shown promising bioactivities such as antioxidative, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative effects, making them attractive candidates for wound management. This study aimed to develop and evaluate tannic acid-based hydrogels containing gallic acid nanoemulsion (GA-NE) and chlorogenic acid (CGA) for accelerating the wound healing performance. Hydrogels were synthesized and characterized using DLS, FESEM, swelling, degradation, thermal, and rheological analyses. In vivo studies included wound contraction rate, histological assessments, hydroxyproline content, oxidative stress markers (MDA, GSH, TAC), and gene expression analysis (TNF-α, TGF-β, VEGF, FGF2, IL11B) on days 3, 7, and 10 post-injuries. Mupirocin® ointment and untreated groups were used as controls. TA/GA-NE/CGA hydrogels showed superior structural integrity, sustained drug release, and improved rheological properties. In vivo, this group demonstrated significantly higher wound contraction, collagen deposition, antioxidant activity, and pro-healing gene expression, while reducing inflammation. Its performance was comparable or superior to mupirocin. The multifunctional polyphenol-based hydrogel represents a promising bioactive wound dressing candidate, potentially promoting healing through oxidative stress regulation, inflammation modulation, and enhanced tissue regeneration. Further preclinical and clinical studies are needed to validate its translational applicability.

articles.title: The phosphodiesterase 4B inhibitor A33 blocks locomotor stimulation by low doses of ethanol and diazepam.
articles.abstract: Nonselective phosphodiesterase type 4 (PDE4) inhibitors (subtypes A-D) such as apremilast significantly reduce voluntary ethanol consumption. The PDE4B inhibitor A33 does not alter apremilast-mediated reductions in drinking but does alter recovery from intoxicating doses of ethanol in C57BL/6J mice. Here, we used A33 to test the hypothesis that PDE4B modulates the effects of low doses of ethanol. A33 (1 mg/kg, i.p.) prevented locomotor stimulation induced by 1.25 and 1.5 g/kg ethanol during the daytime, when mouse activity is normally low, and blocked stimulation by 1.25 g/kg ethanol in the open field. In other behavioral tests, A33 prevented the motivation to escape a stressful situation (hole-board test) and exploratory activity by 1.25 g/kg ethanol (spontaneous alternation test). However, A33 did not alter the anxiolytic effect of 1.25 g/kg ethanol in the elevated plus maze or working memory in the spontaneous alternation test. Similarly, A33 prevented locomotor stimulation by low-dose diazepam (1 mg/kg, i.p.) without altering its anxiolytic effect. Neurochemically, A33 blocked ethanol-evoked dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens, consistent with the behavioral finding that it blocks ethanol-induced locomotor stimulation. Together with evidence that A33 accelerates recovery from intoxication without altering acute tolerance or metabolism, these findings suggest that A33 specifically blocks the stimulant-like properties of low-dose ethanol. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Apremilast nonselectively inhibits phosphodiesterase type 4 (PDE4) subtypes A-D and reduces alcohol drinking in preclinical and human studies. We use subtype-selective inhibitors to identify the subtype(s) driving anti-drinking effects. The PDE4B inhibitor A33 blocked motor stimulation by low-dose alcohol, which may explain its ability to shorten intoxication. A33 also blocked alcohol-induced dopamine release in a central area of the brain's reward system. A33 may prevent stimulatory behaviors associated with alcohol-induced euphoria in humans, which may reduce drinking.

articles.title: Identification of TAS2R-targeting bioactive compounds against metabolic decline: A novel ex vivo methodology based on enteroendocrine and inflammatory readouts.
articles.abstract: Obesity and ageing disrupt intestinal homeostasis. Bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) regulate gut hormone secretion and inflammatory responses. This study aimed to identify intestinal TAS2Rs most affected by obesity and ageing and characterise their receptor-specific responses in ex vivo intestinal explants from Wistar rats. We have integrated previously published transcriptomic and metabolic datasets to identify intestinal TAS2R subtypes differentially modulated by obesity, ageing, and the combination of obesity and ageing. Receptor selection was based on associations with inflammatory, metabolic and enteroendocrine readouts. Subtype-selective agonists were identified through ligand affinity databases and literature screening, and their functional effects were characterised ex vivo in jejunal and ileal explants from Wistar rats. Enterohormone assays revealed receptor- and dose-dependent effects on GLP-1, GIP and CCK secretion, including both stimulatory and inhibitory responses. In Dextran Sulphate Sodium (DSS)-inflamed tissue, bitter agonists exerted divergent immunomodulatory effects on TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-18. Overall, rTas2r108, rTas2r119, rTas2r140 and rTas2r143, activated by amarogentin, costunolide, resveratrol and ethylpyrazine, respectively, emerged as functionally relevant targets. This study establishes an ex vivo platform for profiling intestinal TAS2R agonists, revealing subtype-specific effects on enterohormonal and inflammatory responses. This framework supports the identification of receptor-selective agonists to modulate gut homeostasis in obesity and ageing.

articles.title: Evaluation of deuterium isotope effects on the metabolism of 10 drugs across multiple human cytochrome P450 enzymes: considerations for drug design.
articles.abstract: The phenomenon of deuterium kinetic isotope effects has been occasionally leveraged to design new drugs that have altered drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics relative to their nondeuterated versions. However, it is difficult to know a priori which drugs and exploratory drug candidates would benefit from this drug design strategy. To address this, 10 drugs (amodiaquine, astemizole, cravacitinib, dextromethorphan, ezlopitant, febuxostat, glyburide, linezolid, naproxen, and rosiglitazone) and their deuterated analogs were systematically evaluated for kinetic isotope effects on their metabolism catalyzed by several cytochrome P450 enzymes. Trends could be observed for reaction type in that isotope effects could be observed for some hydroxylation and O-dealkylation reactions, but not for amine N-dealkylation reactions. No trends were apparent across the enzymes and substrates in that the same enzyme could show meaningful isotope effects for some drugs but not others, and substrates could show isotope effects catalyzed by some enzymes and not others. Thus, when considering leveraging deuteration as a drug design strategy intended to alter the metabolism and/or pharmacokinetics of a compound, at this time it cannot be predicted whether a suitable effect will be gained, and evaluation will depend on synthesizing and testing deuterated analogs. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Deuteration has become a strategy in drug design. In this study, it is demonstrated that for some substrates, P450 enzymes, and reaction types, deuterium isotope effects that would meaningfully impact drug clearance can be observed while for others this is not the case.

articles.title: Monocarboxylate transporter 6 mediates sex-dependent cisplatin ototoxicity via metabolite uptake.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin is a widely used anticancer drug, but up to 75% of patients develop ototoxicity, for which there are no fully effective preventive or curative therapies. Although genetic variation in the monocarboxylate transporter 6 (MCT6; SLC16A5) has been associated with reduced cisplatin-induced hearing loss, these findings have not been consistently replicated, and the underlying mechanism has remained unclear. We hypothesized that MCT6 mediates uptake of a cytotoxic cisplatin metabolite and that loss of MCT6 confers protection from cisplatin-induced ototoxicity. Here we show that MCT6 selectively mediates uptake of the cisplatin metabolite N-acetyl-L-cysteine-cisplatin and drives sex-dependent ototoxicity in vivo. Using genetic, pharmacokinetic, and functional auditory approaches, we demonstrate that Mct6 deficiency does not alter systemic platinum exposure but provides robust protection from cisplatin-induced hearing loss in female, but not male, mice. Consistent with this phenotype, Mct6 expression is higher in female cochleae, and MCT6 overexpression increases cellular platinum accumulation following exposure to N-acetyl-L-cysteine-cisplatin but not cisplatin. Together, these findings identify MCT6 as a sex-dependent regulator of cisplatin ototoxicity through selective transport of a toxic platinum metabolite. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies MCT6 (SLC16A5) as a sex-dependent regulator of cisplatin ototoxicity by mediating cochlear transport of a toxic cisplatin metabolite, revealing a novel mechanism to reduce toxicity without altering systemic platinum exposure.

articles.title: Hinokitiol alleviates neuropathic pain and modulates Nrf2/HO-1 and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.
articles.abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) is a chronic and debilitating condition that results from peripheral or central nervous system injury and is characterized by hyperalgesia and abnormal pain sensations. Current treatments are often ineffective and associated with significant side effects. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of hinokitiol (HIK) in chronic constriction injury (CCI)-induced NP and examined its association with oxidative stress and neuroinflammatory signaling. Network pharmacology identified NFE2L2 (Nrf2) as a candidate node, while molecular docking predicted a possible HIK-Nrf2 interaction; these computational findings were used for hypothesis generation rather than as evidence of direct physical binding. In vivo, HIK significantly alleviated mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia in CCI rats, reduced spinal microglial activation, and decreased markers associated with NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptotic signaling. In LPS/ATP-stimulated BV2 cells, HIK promoted Nrf2 nuclear accumulation and HO-1 expression, reduced ROS accumulation, and attenuated inflammasome- and pyroptosis-associated markers. Pharmacological Nrf2 inhibition with ML385 partially weakened the effects of HIK, supporting the involvement, but not exclusive mediation, of Nrf2 signaling. Collectively, the findings indicate that the analgesic effects of HIK are associated with modulation of the Nrf2/HO-1 and NLRP3 inflammasome-related pathways. Further target-engagement, pathway-specific rescue, sex-inclusive, and primary-cell studies are required to establish direct molecular targets and causal cell-specific mechanisms.

articles.title: Sex-related differences in outcomes following psilocybin or escitalopram: a Bayesian secondary analysis.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Major depressive disorder (MDD) shows marked sex differences in prevalence, symptomatology, and treatment response. However, females remain underrepresented in many clinical trials, and sex-specific treatment outcomes are rarely examined. OBJECTIVES: This study reanalyzed data from a randomized controlled trial comparing psilocybin and escitalopram for MDD to evaluate sex differences across multiple psychological domains. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc Bayesian analysis of a six-week, double-blind trial in adults with moderate-to-severe MDD (N = 59; 20 female; psilocybin n = 30, 11 female; escitalopram n = 29, 9 female). Post-treatment depression, anhedonia, anxiety, thought suppression, and well-being were modeled by sex, treatment, sex-by-treatment interaction, and baseline score. Sexual dysfunction, measured post-treatment only, was analyzed ordinally. Prior-sensitivity analyses used narrower and wider priors. RESULTS: No outcome showed an overall sex difference across treatments. Within psilocybin, females had lower post-treatment anxiety than males (STAI adjusted difference = -8.77, 95% CrI = -15.73 to -1.73; BFany = 11.18), although the estimate varied across priors and the narrowest prior included zero. The sex-by-treatment interaction was inconclusive (difference=-8.62, 95% CrI=-18.36 to 1.30; BFany = 2.55). A directional female advantage in anhedonia with escitalopram was unsupported by Bayes factors. No sex differences emerged on depression scales. Among males, sexual dysfunction was lower with psilocybin than with escitalopram. Within escitalopram, females reported less sexual dysfunction than males. CONCLUSIONS: This reanalysis identified sex-related patterns in anxiety under psilocybin but no clear treatment-specific interaction. Findings support adequately powered, sex-balanced trials incorporating hormonal and reproductive factors.

articles.title: Evaluating whether a therapeutic dose of ketamine exposure during adolescence influences adult vulnerability in rats to commonly abused drugs.
articles.abstract: Rationale Ketamine has emerged as a rapid-acting antidepressant drug for treatment-resistant depression in adults and is currently evaluated for adolescent depression. However, the long-term effects of ketamine exposure during this period of brain development remain unclear, particularly regarding addiction liability. Objectives To investigate whether repeated ketamine exposure during adolescence may influence the long-term risk of addiction following subsequent exposure to commonly abused drugs (alcohol and cocaine) in adulthood. Methods Male and female Sprague-Dawley rats received daily i.p. injections of ketamine (10 mg/kg) or saline for 7 consecutive days during mid adolescence. The dose paradigm of ketamine administered was selected based on its antidepressant-like properties in adolescent rats. In adulthood, addiction liability was measured by voluntary ethanol consumption, using a two-bottle choice paradigm, and by assessing cocaine reward using a single-exposure place preference protocol. Results The main results suggested that a therapeutic dose of ketamine exposure during adolescence did not enhance addictive liability in adulthood as measured by voluntary ethanol consumption or cocaine reward in rats of both sexes. Conclusions Ketamine, administered during adolescence at a dose known to induce antidepressant-like effects did not impact the long-term risk of addiction caused by exposure to commonly abused drugs (i.e., alcohol and cocaine). These results suggested a good long-term safety profile following the therapeutic use of ketamine in adolescence.

articles.title: Factors Influencing Powder Compressibility: Mechanistic Insights for Robust Pharmaceutical Tablet Manufacturing.
articles.abstract: Compressibility is a critical material attribute in tablet manufacturing, as it governs powder densification, inter-particulate bonding, and the mechanical integrity of solid oral dosage forms. Intrinsic solid-state properties such as polymorphism, crystal structure, molecular packing, slip planes, and hardness influence the primary mechanism for deformation and ultimately determine whether materials undergo plastic deformation, elastic deformation, or brittle fracture during compaction. These effects are controlled by the properties of the particles and surface properties. Factors such as particle size and shape, surface free energy, particle aggregation, density, and flow affect the development of the contact area and the transmission of stress within the tablet. Environmental conditions and processing parameters also alter these fundamental responses, thereby affecting densification efficiency, tensile strength, and defect formation. Compressibility, compactibility, and tabletability are determined by these interrelated factors, which ultimately influence manufacturability and product robustness. This review emphasizes the importance of a holistic understanding of the mechanisms governing API compressibility by integrating solid-state properties, compaction behavior, and empirical modeling techniques. It highlights how these interconnected factors influence powder desnsification, mechanical strength, and tablet performance, providing a scientific framework for the rational design and optimization of pharmaceutical formulations. Furthermore, the concept discussed in this review may facilitate the application of Quality by Design(QbD) principles and support the development of robust manufacturing strategies for solid oral dosage forms.

articles.title: ICH Q3C Revisited Part II: Safety Assessments for Three Acetal Residual Solvents.
articles.abstract: In ICH Q3C, first released in 1997, nine residual solvents are described as "solvents for which no adequate toxicological data was found". Nearly thirty years later the same nine solvents lie "abandoned" in ICH Q3C (R9) in spite of the fact that, in most cases, sufficient toxicological data are now available to support an adequate risk assessment. The solvents in question represent several chemical types: three are acetals, two are haloacids, two are hydrocarbons, plus one ketone and one ether. This article concerns the three acetals which are all considered to be of low toxicity.

articles.title: A comparative analysis of the EPA's 2005 cancer risk assessment restructuring vs. the historical Crump linearized multistage model.
articles.abstract: In 2005, the US EPA finalized its Guidelines for Carcinogen Risk Assessment, transitioning from the 1986 Linearized Multistage (LMS) framework to the Benchmark Dose (). This shift leveraged software to fit empirical curves to biological data, with a focus on chronic animal bioassay cancer studies. This paper conducts a meta-analysis evaluating the "before and after" risk metrics for 28 carcinogens during this transition. These findings demonstrate that for linear extrapolations, the exposure limits generated by the consistently land within a single log-scale factor () of LMS estimates for 89.3% of chemicals (25 of 28). Furthermore, 64.3% of the cohort (18 of 28) exhibits near numerical parity (), with several agents showing equivalence. We show that cases of divergence () are driven by changes in biological inputs (e.g., human vs. animal datasets, multi-organ tumor aggregation) rather than low-dose curve-fitting. While this restructuring offers theoretically improved model data fits for sublinear and threshold carcinogens, the findings indicate that the BMD approach, like the LMS model, is still primarily limited by the use of the few-dose/high-dose NTP protocol. The present findings are in close agreement with previous studies comparing LMS and BMD risk estimates for a wide range of EPA carcinogens.

articles.title: Snake venom toxins in cancer therapy: advances in targeted delivery and peptide design.
articles.abstract: Snake venom represents a potent biological arsenal of cytotoxic compounds. Venom proteins and peptides, including disintegrins, venomous enzymes, three-finger toxins, and serine proteases, have garnered attention as effective anticancer agents. Despite their efficacy at nano- or micromolar concentrations, non-standardized mixtures often limit their therapeutic utilization, necessitating fractionation to minimize side effects. This review examines the antitumor potential of snake venom and its constituent proteins and peptides through a literature search in NCBI PubMed. We highlight the antitumor efficacies of venom polypeptides by correlating them with IC50 values across various cell lines, demonstrating micromolar cytotoxic concentrations. The review encompasses several key areas: whole venom antitumor efficacy, mechanisms of action of individual proteins and peptides, fractionation and purification methods, cytotoxic effects of low molecular weight peptides, and delivery system approaches utilizing peptide sequences as cell-penetrating mechanisms alongside liposomes and nanoparticles for enhanced polypeptide toxicity. Given that cilengitide contains an RGD sequence analogous to disintegrins and targets integrins, we provide a dedicated analysis of its anticancer potential and clinical trial outcomes. Clinical evidence indicates the necessity for further investigation into the synergistic effects of cilengitide with established chemotherapeutic agents. The scientific data reviewed demonstrate that antimetastatic properties constitute the most extensively studied mechanism of venom polypeptides. This review underscores the therapeutic promise of venom-derived polypeptides while emphasizing the critical need for advanced delivery systems and rigorous clinical validation to translate these findings into viable cancer therapeutics.

articles.title: Physicochemical Characterization and In Vitro Evaluation of Praziquantel-loaded Oleogels for Oral Drug Delivery.
articles.abstract: Oral delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs such as praziquantel (PZQ) is frequently limited by poor absorption and low bioavailability. Lipid-based carriers represent a promising strategy, as their matrices enhance solubility by incorporating hydrophobic molecules within a lipophilic environment. In this study, PZQ-loaded beeswax (BW) oleogels were formulated using palm oil (PO) or cottonseed oil (CSO) as lipid carriers, followed by physicochemical characterisation and in vitro studies. We hypothesised that differences in oil composition would influence the structure and physicochemical properties of BW oleogels, affecting drug release, in vitro digestion behaviour, and intestinal permeation. BW oleogels exhibited gelation at a critical concentration of 5% (w/w), resulting in a high oil-binding capacity of at least 98%. Microscopy and X-ray diffraction indicated concentration-dependent development of a dense, needle-like semi-crystalline network, while rheological analysis confirmed stable gel behaviour (G' > G″). For the first time, we demonstrate the application of a modified everted gut sac model, adapted to quantitatively investigate the intestinal interaction and permeation behaviour of PZQ-loaded oleogels. Simulated in vitro digestion revealed negligible release under salivary conditions and limited gastric release (< 16%), followed by a bioaccessible fraction of 52-57%. The BW oleogels exhibited reduced intestinal permeation relative to the free drug, indicating drug entrapment within the oleogel, while oleogel-intestinal tissue interaction remained below 7.8%. These findings highlight the potential of BW oleogels as oral carriers for hydrophobic compounds such as PZQ and suggest their applicability as modified-release delivery systems.

articles.title: Benchmark Dose Analysis of Ames Test Data: Identifying Appropriate Benchmark Response Values and Modeling Approaches.
articles.abstract: As interest in the quantitative interpretation of genotoxicity assay data continues to grow, the Ames bacterial mutagenicity assay offers a valuable opportunity due to its long-standing use and extensive dose-response data sets. A key challenge for the quantitative use of this data is determining how best to apply benchmark dose (BMD) analysis to Ames data to support a quantitative risk assessment. This requires careful selection of both an appropriate benchmark response (BMR) and the most suitable modeling approach. Using a database of Ames bacterial mutagenicity test data from regulatory submissions, we evaluate a range of BMRs and several benchmark modeling approaches. Our evaluation indicates that a 50% increase in revertants over the background (BMR50) is a justifiable, interpretable candidate BMR for Ames studies in the pesticides regulatory context. Furthermore, in the filtered Ames-positive data set, the Bayesian implementations (BMABMDR Laplace approximation and Bridge sampling) yielded BMDLs that met the EFSA criteria for use as a reference point for a larger proportion of data sets and had narrower confidence intervals than the PROAST implementation. Together, these findings provide a practical framework for deriving Ames-based potency estimates to support chemical prioritization, read-across, and quantitative weight-of-evidence assessment.

articles.title: A framework to characterize uncertainty for dose extrapolation from in vitro bioassays.
articles.abstract: New approach methods (NAMs) can accelerate chemical assessment and reduce reliance on animal testing, but their application requires quantitative extrapolation of bioactive in vitro concentrations to equivalent in vivo doses. Confidence in quantitative in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (Q-IVIVE) is impacted by uncertainty in both the in vitro concentration and the toxicokinetic parameters used for reverse dosimetry. We propose a framework to: (1) define the processes used to derive an administered equivalent dose (AED); (2) identify uncertainty sources; (3) characterize uncertainty in the data and models; and (4) propagate these uncertainties to the AED. The framework distinguishes nominal assay concentrations from blood- or plasma-equivalent concentrations that account for chemical disposition and compositional differences between in vitro and in vivo media. Parameter-specific uncertainty factors can be derived from experimental variability, model performance statistics, simulations, or expert judgement and combined using a semi-probabilistic approach. Illustrative chemical-space analyses show that nominal and blood-equivalent concentrations may be comparable for some hydrophilic, non-volatile chemicals but can differ by more than two orders of magnitude for hydrophobic or volatile chemicals. The framework provides a systematic, and tiered basis for evaluating confidence in calculated Q-IVIVE doses and supports the application of NAM data in chemical hazard and risk assessment. Ongoing chemical-specific case studies will evaluate implementation of the framework, verify the validity of the simplifying assumptions, and identify opportunities for refinement.

articles.title: The effect of repeated administration of lumateperone on cytochrome P450 expression and activity in rat liver.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Antipsychotic drugs are used for long-term treatment of schizophrenia and other psychotic-related symptoms. Our present work aimed at investigating the effects of chronic administration of the third-generation antipsychotic drug lumateperone on the expression of cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes involved in drug metabolism and transcription factors in rat liver. METHODS: Male Wistar rats received lumateperone (1 mg/kg) once daily for 14 days. 24 h after the last dose, their livers were excised, and CYP enzyme expression and activity were measured. In addition, the expression of transcription factors and serum hormone concentrations were evaluated. RESULTS: Lumateperone significantly increased the CYP expression and/or activity of CYP2A, CYP2B, and CYP3A enzymes, but decreased that of CYP2D enzymes. The observed changes in CYP enzymes were in line with alterations in transcription factors: lumateperone elevated the mRNA level of PXR and reduced that of FXR in the liver. Simultaneously, increased corticosterone levels and decreased T4 levels in serum were observed. CONCLUSION: Repeated lumateperone administration modulated the expression and activity of selected hepatic CYP enzymes in rats. These findings indicate biological effects on hepatic drug-metabolizing pathways in a rat model. Relevance to human drug-drug interactions remains to be established in in vitro pharmacokinetic studies.

articles.title: Neuropsychiatric adverse event reporting with GLP-1-based therapies: a post-marketing pharmacovigilance analysis using the WHO global individual case safety report database (VigiBase).
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Concerns regarding neuropsychiatric adverse events (NPAEs), including depression and suicidality, have emerged with the expanding use of GLP-1-based therapies across metabolic and weight-management indications. This study aimed to characterize neuropsychiatric adverse-event reporting patterns for GLP-1-based therapies in VigiBase using disproportionality analysis. METHODS: Individual case safety reports entered into the WHO global pharmacovigilance database (VigiBase) from inception through 31 January 2025 were examined. Disproportionality analysis using the information components and the reporting odds ratio was conducted to identify putative safety signals. The full VigiBase reporting background during the study period was used as the comparator. We described the drug-event pairs, mapped signal overlap across agents, evaluated the relationship between reporting frequency and signal magnitude, and conducted stratified analyses by sex and age. RESULTS: Among 899 280 GLP-1RAs-related reports, 19 811 (2.2%) related NPAEs comprised 273 preferred terms and generated 69 positive signals. Semaglutide and liraglutide presented the broadest and most potent signal portfolios, driven chiefly by binge eating (semaglutide, IC₀₂₅ = 3.379; ROR₀₂₅ = 14.483), and aversion (liraglutide, IC₀₂₅ = 3.365; ROR₀₂₅ = 20.512). In contrast, albiglutide was essentially signal negative, and dulaglutide and tirzepatide generated narrower spectra. In addition, semaglutide was positively associated with two "suicide/self-injury" AEs: "depression suicidal" (ROR₀₂₅ = 4.822) and "suicidal ideation" (ROR₀₂₅ = 2.643). CONCLUSIONS: This study identified several potential drug safety signals. However, the estimates were unadjusted and may be influenced by confounding by indication, channelling, notoriety bias, and event competition. Eating-related signals should be interpreted cautiously because they may overlap with the treated population and appetite-related pharmacology of these agents. Given the spontaneous reporting nature of VigiBase, these findings should be interpreted as potential reporting signals rather than evidence of causality. Further well-designed observational studies and prospective clinical investigations are needed to clarify whether GLP-1-based therapies are associated with increased neuropsychiatric risk and to identify patient-level risk modifiers.

articles.title: Identifying Dose-Relevant Covariates With SCOUT: A Case Study of Lorlatinib.
articles.abstract: Molecularly targeted therapeutics, such as lorlatinib, are typically initiated at fixed starting doses with subsequent tolerability-guided modifications, although substantial interindividual variability in pharmacokinetics and drug exposure may influence both efficacy and safety outcomes. Therefore, identifying patient factors associated with individualized dose requirements is an important step toward precision dosing. The aim of this study was to apply the Systematic Covariate Observational Uncovering Technique (SCOUT) framework to explore patient characteristics that may be associated with the individualized optimal dose of lorlatinib. A previously published population pharmacokinetic model was used to estimate individual pharmacokinetic parameters and individualized optimal doses, targeting a trough concentration of 150 ng/mL 3 weeks after treatment initiation. Associations between the estimated optimal dose and patient covariates were examined through exploratory visualization and quantified using multivariate linear regression with Lindeman-Merenda-Gold relative importance analysis. Individualized optimal doses, successfully estimated in all 330 patients, exhibited a wide distribution (mean ± SD: 194 ± 134 mg/day). The exploratory analyses suggested that older age, female sex, and greater renal impairment were associated with lower estimated optimal doses, with sex explaining the largest proportion of the variance. By reframing the covariate analysis around the dose rather than pharmacokinetic parameters, this study provides a clinically interpretable perspective on interindividual variability in dosing requirements. Although exploratory and hypothesis-generating, this study lays a quantitative foundation for future evaluations of precision dosing strategies for lorlatinib.
